01 · THE STORY SO FAR

Same numbers.
Opposite outcomes.

PHASE 1 · SAFE MODEL · EXIT 0

We built one 20-byte shelf with three labeled sections. We placed HELLO (5) inside the 8. We watched ABCDEFGHIJKLMNO (15) spill 7 past the marker. Shown, never written: we capped every copy with min().

LESSON: where we draw the line

PHASE 2 · REAL BUG · EXIT 1

We moved to a real stack buffer: char buffer[8] at [32,40). We called strcpy with no size check: 15 letters plus null made WRITE of size 16. Eight bytes landed past the end. AddressSanitizer reported stack-buffer-overflow at offset 40, then ABORTING.

LESSON: what we risk when we cross it
02 · THE PROBLEM, IN ONE LINE

A copy with no size check.

phase2_vulnerable_strcpy.cpp : 58
char buffer[8];   strcpy(buffer, input);  // no size parameter. copies until '\0'.
input 15 + null = 16into capacity 8⇒ 8 bytes land on the neighbor stack
LAB · DRAG THE INPUT LENGTH
15 charsOVERFLOWS
Write 16 into 8: 8 past the end. This is the red run.
03 · THE FIX

Check. Then copy.

phase3_fixed_copy.cpp · safe
n = min(input.size(), 7);
memcpy(buffer, input, n);   buffer[n] = '\0';
1234567 → n=7 → FITS ABCDEFGHIJKLMNO → n=7 → TRUNCATED SAFELY

Cut by plan, not by accident.
